added_provisions.reason: The map's procedure omits Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (9), a mandatory execution step: the notary must know one of the executants or the two witnesses, or establish the executant's identity from a national identity card, passport bio page or driving licence; he must satisfy himself that the witnesses are of good repute and well acquainted with the testator; and the witnesses must sign a declaration to that effect at the foot of the instrument. The enrichment puts two neighbours forward as witnesses, so the rule is directly engaged and the procedure limb of the answer is incomplete without it. Recorded as supporting, with a procedurally_requires edge from PROV-M021-005.

question_decisions.note: No indispensable provision was rejected or left unresolved, so the question stands as proposed_gold. statute_only is upheld: the age limit is fixed by Wills Ordinance s.2 as substituted by Act No. 29 of 2022, and the procedure by Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.4 as amended by Act No. 30 of 2022 together with Notaries Ordinance s.31; neither limb needs Roman-Dutch common law or a decided case. Two claims were downgraded to disputed, one provision to partially_verified, and one supporting provision was added. The hop count of 3 and the four legal issues were confirmed, and the issues were marked verified.

disagreements.researcher_position: CL-M021-Q01-013: Sunil's chronic illness does not affect his competence under the Ordinance, and because he remains lucid the notary can properly certify his good and sound mind.
disagreements.verifier_position: The first half is right as a statement about the Wills Ordinance, which imposes only an age condition. The second half asserts that the notary can properly certify sound mind, which turns on the substantive test of testamentary capacity. That test is Roman-Dutch common law and is not in the corpus; Notaries Ordinance s.31(20)(h) prescribes the duty to state sound mind but supplies no standard. Marked disputed rather than rejected, because the statutory duty and the physician's fact are both real.

disagreements.researcher_position: CL-M021-Q01-016: only one instrument need be executed and no publication is required during Sunil's lifetime.
disagreements.verifier_position: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.16 excepts wills from the triplicate rule and s.9 removes any need for publication, so both halves point the right way. But s.16 does not positively say that a single instrument suffices, and Notaries Ordinance s.31(24) still requires the notary to preserve as his protocol a draft or copy carrying the signatures of the testator and the witnesses. "Only one instrument need be executed" needs qualification.

unsupported_claims: CL-M021-Q01-013, marked disputed: the assertion that the notary can properly certify good and sound mind rests on a capacity standard that is not in the statutory corpus.

missing_definitions_or_exceptions: Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (9): identity of the executant, and the good repute, acquaintance and foot-of-deed declaration of the witnesses. Added as PROV-M021-901.

Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (11): wills and codicils are excepted from the requirement that the instrument be read over and explained in the presence of the attesting witnesses. The researcher considered and excluded it; it is a genuine will-specific exception and a plausible mark-earning point, so it is flagged rather than added.

Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (22): the notary may not attest outside the area, or in a language other than that, in which he is authorised to practise. The enrichment makes Mr Perera a Colombo District Sinhala-language notary attending at Nugegoda, which is consistent, but the map never records the constraint.

Notaries Ordinance s.31 rules (23) and (24): consecutive numbering of wills, preservation of the protocol, and the rule that for wills and codicils only the number and date go in the register. Relevant to the procedure limb and to CL-M021-Q01-016.

Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (15A): thumb impression on the original, duplicate and protocol for an instrument in respect of immovable property. How it interacts with a will devising land, given the s.16 exception, cannot be resolved on the corpus text and is left for the lawyer.
case_law_dependence: The answer cites no case law and the validator's case-citation regex is clean.
The only real pull towards case law is testamentary capacity, a sound and disposing mind. It is already recorded in corpus_gaps and is not what the question asks, so statute_only is upheld.

But three added facts telegraph the answer: FACT-M021-Q01-002 says Sunil can place a thumb impression, which points straight at the 2022 formality that is the point of the question; FACT-M021-Q01-004 supplies a notary; FACT-M021-Q01-005 states that neither witness nor either spouse takes a benefit, which is the whole of Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.11. A candidate could recover much of the procedure from the facts alone.
